abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cisplatin is a platinum compound that has revolutionized the treatment of various solid organ tumors. Cisplatin is associated with a variety of side effects and has recently been indicted in the development of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome is a potentially reversible condition, with the mainstay of therapy being correction of the underlying cause and withdrawal of the offending drug. However, there are no clear guidelines regarding the possibility of subsequent re-treatment with the causative agent. CASE PRESENTATION: A 23-year-old Asian man presented to our Emergency Department with a four-month history of concomitant abdominal pain and backache and a two-week history of left-sided leg swelling. Diagnostic investigations revealed bilateral pulmonary embolism, extensive deep venous thrombosis and widespread lung and liver metastatic deposits with abdomino-pelvic lymphadenopathy. His biopsy and tumor markers were consistent with non-seminomatous germ cell tumor and he was subsequently started on an initial cycle of cisplatin and etoposide chemotherapy. On the second day of treatment he developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome clinically and radiologically. Cisplatin was stopped for the next two days while etoposide was continued, resulting in complete resolution of his symptoms. He was re-challenged with cisplatin on day five of chemotherapy because a platin-based chemotherapy regimen was his only hope of potential cure. He tolerated it well, with no recurrence of his neurological symptoms and the remainder of his in-patient stay remained uneventful. He was discharged on day eight. He has since then completed treatment and is currently in remission. CONCLUSIONS: The occurrence of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome after cisplatin use has been well reported in the literature. We strongly believe that our patient also developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome secondary to cisplatin. The uniqueness of our patient's case lies in the successful re-treatment of our patient with the offending drug. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first instance where a patient was successfully re-treated with cisplatin after having developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome as a result of cisplatin use. The excellent response to re-treatment without recurrence of neurological symptoms in our patient's case provides insight into re-treatment as an option in scenarios where treatment options are limited.

**はじめに**
シスプラチンは白金系化合物であり、様々な固形腫瘍の治療を一変させた。シスプラチンには多様な副作用があり、近年は可逆性後頭葉白質脳症症候群の発症への関与も指摘されている。可逆性後頭葉白質脳症症候群は可逆性の病態であり、基礎となる原因の是正と原因薬剤の中止が治療の基本である。しかし、原因薬剤による再治療の可能性についての明確なガイドラインはない。

**症例提示**
23歳のアジア人男性が、4か月前からの腹痛と背部痛、2週間前からの左下肢の腫脹を主訴に救急部を受診した。精査により、両側肺動脈塞栓症、広範な深部静脈血栓症、肺と肝臓の広範な転移巣、腹骨盤部リンパ節腫大が判明した。生検と腫瘍マーカーの所見から非セミノーマ性胚細胞腫瘍と診断され、シスプラチンとエトポシドによる化学療法を開始した。治療2日目に臨床的および画像的に可逆性後頭葉白質脳症症候群を発症した。シスプラチンを2日間中止し、エトポシドを継続したところ、症状は完全に消失した。白金系化合物を基本とする化学療法レジメンが根治の唯一の望みであったため、治療5日目にシスプラチンを再投与した。忍容性は良好で、神経症状の再発はなく、治療8日目に退院した。その後治療を完遂し、現在寛解中である。

**結論**
シスプラチン使用後の可逆性後頭葉白質脳症症候群は文献上よく報告されている。我々は、本患者の症状がシスプラチンによる続発性の可逆性後頭葉白質脳症症候群であったと強く考えている。本症例の特徴は、原因薬剤による再治療に成功した点である。我々の知る限り、シスプラチンによる可逆性後頭葉白質脳症症候群を発症した後、シスプラチンで再治療に成功した初めての症例である。神経症状の再発なく良好な反応が得られたことは、治療選択肢が限られる状況における再治療の選択肢を示唆する。
